question.problem: Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}]$, find a basis of $\text{Null}(A).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $A$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation $Ax=0$ is equivalent to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

This implies that the only solution of $Ax=0$ is $x=0.$ So, $\text{Null}(A)={0},$ which means that the basis of $\text{Null}(A)$ is the empty set, i.e., $B={\,}.$
